text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.9% today, continuing a sharp two-week decline of 13.5%. The slide reflects mounting geopolitical tension in the Middle East and broader energy supply concerns: Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure, Iranian tanker incidents in the Strait of Hormuz, and ongoing Russia-Ukraine refinery strikes all threaten oil transport and production stability. These disruptions, combined with crude prices holding steady around $82 domestically but rising globally to $91.80, create uncertainty about refining margins and fuel demand that refiners depend on.

Refineries are running near full capacity at 97.5%, which normally supports strong margins, but the stock's decline suggests investors are pricing in that geopolitical risk could disrupt the smooth flow of crude oil to U.S. refineries or demand for refined products. The fact that oil storage remains relatively high (692 million barrels) may also signal concern that demand could soften if global tensions escalate further.
